question: Run K-means (k=3) 50 times using random_state=42 as the master seed. Build a consensus matrix where entry [i,j] is the fraction of runs in which samples i and j were co-clustered. Visualize it as a heatmap.

comparison_details.explanation: Both images show a symmetric 120-by-120 sample co-assignment matrix using a heatmap with a 0-to-1 color scale. They exhibit the same scientific structure: three strong high-consensus diagonal cluster blocks, low consensus between most clusters, and a small set of less stable samples producing intermediate-valued rows and columns. The apparent block locations differ because the reference largely retains an index-based ordering, placing unstable samples near the final indices, whereas the candidate explicitly reorders samples using average-linkage clustering of 1 minus consensus. This permutation groups related and unstable samples differently but does not change the underlying pairwise information. The candidate also provides more descriptive sample labels, a detailed title identifying k=3, 50 runs, and master seed 42, and a labeled colorbar; the reference uses numeric indices and a generic title. These are presentation and ordering differences rather than substantive data differences, so the plots convey the same scientific result.
